claims.text: ML-TI+FEP can reproduce solid and liquid free energies while retaining vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–phonon coupling.
ML-TI+FEP can achieve more than a 10× speedup relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
ML-TI+FEP can achieve a 2–5× speedup relative to TOR-TILD.
ML-TI+FEP can maintain free-energy errors below 5 meV/atom.
An actively trained machine-learned interatomic potential will be used as a surrogate for ab initio dynamics in both solid and liquid phases.
Thermodynamic integration on the machine-learned potential will be used to obtain the free-energy change.
Free-energy perturbation corrections will be applied at a small number of temperature–pressure points using short ab initio MD runs.
The machine-learned potential will be trained on ab initio snapshots selected on the fly.
The machine-learned potential accurately captures the potential-energy surface in both solid and liquid phases.
The machine-learned potential accurately captures anharmonic fluctuations in both phases.
Replacing most ab initio dynamics with machine-learned-potential sampling drastically reduces sampling cost.
Targeted ab initio free-energy corrections keep systematic errors below the proposed accuracy threshold.
The method is proposed to apply to alloys containing up to four elements.
The proposed temperature range is 0.8–1.2 times the melting temperature.
The proposed pressure range is below 5 GPa.
The predicted free-energy uncertainty is ±2 meV/atom.
The predicted speedup may vary by ±20%.
A comparison against full ab initio MD will measure solid–liquid free energies, latent heat, and melting-point shift for Ni–Al and a quaternary high-entropy alloy.

contradictions.description: The claimed fidelity is below 5 meV/atom, but the method is only falsified when deviation from explicit ab initio results exceeds 10 meV/atom. Results between 5 and 10 meV/atom would violate the stated performance claim without satisfying the stated falsification rule.
The hypothesis predicts a speedup greater than 10× over explicit ab initio MD, whereas the predicted-outcome field states a factor-of-10 reduction. This is a minor boundary inconsistency.
